Resolves #20884

The Planning arrangement gains its **Team board** (`Workstation.view.BoardPane`, a `Neo.board.Container`), bound to the `workItems` instance the Team schedule reads. A card moved on the board is one `record.set({status, order})`, and the schedule's bar shows it in its status colour. A bar moved in the schedule is one `record.set({startDate, endDate})`, and the card shows the new days. Both hold in one window and with the schedule popped out into a second one. A card names its days in the planning calendar's format and its person from the provider's `people` store. Each column wears the colour the schedule gives its status's bars.

Evidence: L3 (local headless Chromium on the real Workstation: a pointer drag and keyboard moves on the board, keyboard bar moves in the schedule, a pop-out into a second window, reloads of both windows, each record read back from the App Worker) → L3 required (browser-observable ACs).

## Deltas from ticket

- **The plan is the board's neighbour tab, above the schedule.** At 1600×1000 three stacked panes cannot each show their content: the board needs ~340 px for three cards per column, the schedule ~335 px for six people, the plan ~480 px for fifteen rows, of ~860 px. So the two views of one set of work items show together and whole, and the plan's tab stands above the schedule on the same calendar, its weeks still in line. The split is 0.58 / 0.42.
- **A card's footer: days and person.** An app card item (`workstation-plan`) shows the days through `planningCalendar`'s new `daysLabel`, which names as the last day the UTC day the exclusive end's last moment falls on, so an end the schedule's editor saves at noon names its own day. It shows the person through the family's own avatar item. Both time axes and the cards now name a day through one function, `dayLabel`.
- **One colour per status across the desk.** A column wears its bars' colour; a unit arm pins the board's column map to the schedule's `statusBarCls`. A card's progress bar and a bar's progress fill take that colour too, so amber, violet and emerald stay themselves under the fill.
- **The plan is not a status.** A `plan-tokens` bridge gives the Gantt pane solid slate bars, darker phases, signal milestones and ink links. Without it, its default sky and amber read as Ready and In progress.
- **The board joins the instrument's palette** through a `board-tokens` bridge beside the grid and timeline bridges in `Viewport.scss`, the sheet both boot modes load. Columns are 300 px, so five fill the desk. A column body is a container, which the theme paints in the page's neutral ground, so it is made transparent. Tree guide lines take the instrument's line colour in every grid.
- **A card's editor offers the work item's own fields** through the board's `fields` config (#21222, merged with #21224): title, status, the person as a select over the team, progress and description. A work item's days stay with the schedule, which moves them.
- **The caption, the README and the two time panes' JSDoc** describe the new layout.
